description: EAGLE 9.6 editor commands RUN through WRITE from the built-in help (alphabetical command reference): running ULPs and scripts, highlighting, signals and netlists, smd pads and arrays, splines, slicing and splitting lines, smashing name/value texts, technologies, texts and text variables, undo, library update and use, values, assembly variants, vias, zoom/pan and saving (including EAGLE 7 format and design blocks). In the syntax, capital words are keywords, lowercase words are values, | separates alternatives, .. means repeatable and • stands for a mouse click, written as (x y) in the current GRID unit in scripts.

tools.name: RUN
tools.description: Starts a User Language Program (.ulp) in the current schematic, board or library editor; optional arguments are passed to the program in the builtin variables argc and argv. ULPs read the design data, write files and can hand a command string back to the editor with exit("..."), so RUN is the bridge between scripted commands and program-generated operations.

parameters.name: file_name
parameters.description: ULP file to execute.

parameters.name: argument
parameters.description: Optional arguments, available in the ULP as argv[1] ... (argc counts them).

tools.example:
RUN bom.ulp;
RUN myexport.ulp arg1 arg2;
tools.notes: When started from a context menu, the clicked object is put into a group that the ULP can test with ingroup(); for wires the group bits tell which end point was selected; a previously defined group becomes invalid. In a script, a ULP that returns a non-zero value (via exit() or the STOP button) terminates the script. SET CONTEXT can add a RUN entry to an object's context menu. Related: SCRIPT.

tools.name: SCRIPT
tools.description: Executes a script file, i.e. a sequence of EAGLE editor commands, in the current editor. Use it to customize EAGLE (menus, key assignments, colors, grid) or to build and modify designs from generated data such as board outlines, part placements or netlists. When typed without extension, .scr is assumed.

parameters.name: file_name
parameters.description: Script file; without extension '.scr' is appended, a trailing '.' means 'no extension' (SCRIPT myscr. runs the file myscr).

tools.notes: Selected with the mouse, SCRIPT shows a list of all .scr files. EXPORT can write scripts from existing data. In the library editor all layers are recognized only if the library editor has been loaded before. A ULP started with RUN inside a script aborts the script when it returns non-zero. See also 'Script file format (.scr)' and 'SCRIPT eagle.scr and editor labels'. Related: SET, MENU, ASSIGN, EXPORT, RUN.

tools.name: Script file format (.scr)
tools.description: A script is a plain text file of editor commands written with the normal command syntax, one or more commands per line, each terminated by ';' when it has fewer than the maximum number of options. Lines starting with '#' are comments, and a '\' at the end of a line makes sure the first word of the next line is not taken as a command, so long parameter lists can continue. Mouse clicks are written as coordinates (x y) in the current GRID unit.

parameters.name: (x y)
parameters.description: Coordinate in the current GRID unit; units can be appended per value, e.g. (100mil 200mil); allowed units mm, mic, mil, in.
Current mouse cursor position.

parameters.name: coordinate modifiers
parameters.description: After '(' : > right click, A Alt, C Ctrl, S Shift, R relative to the mark, P polar (radius, angle) relative to the mark, e.g. (CR> 1 2).

parameters.name: abbreviations
parameters.description: Commands and keywords may be shortened as long as they stay unambiguous (CHA LAY TO = CHANGE LAYER TOP).

tools.notes: Always use '.' as decimal separator in scripts (a comma only works with matching locale settings). Dialogs that would stop a script can be answered automatically with SET CONFIRM YES / NO / OPTn around the specific command. Text parameters with blanks or ';' must be in single quotes. Keywords are not case sensitive.

tools.name: SCRIPT eagle.scr (default settings) and editor labels
tools.description: If a script named eagle.scr exists in the project directory or in the script path, it is executed every time a drawing is loaded into an editor window (and when the drawing type changes in a library). Labels at the beginning of a line (SCH:, BRD:, LBR:, DEV:, PAC:, SYM:) mark sections so that only the part for the current editor type runs, up to the next label. This is the place for per-editor grids, menus, key assignments and SET options.
tools.usage:
SCH:
  commands for the schematic editor
BRD:
  commands for the board editor
LBR:  DEV:  PAC:  SYM:
  commands for library, device, package and symbol editing

parameters.name: EDITOR:
parameters.description: One of SCH, BRD, LBR, DEV, PAC, SYM followed by ':' at the start of a line.

tools.notes: The default eagle.scr in Documents/EAGLE/scripts can include SCRIPT default-assign.scr (uncomment it) to define the default keyboard shortcuts. The command-line option -C of eagle.exe does not run eagle.scr. Menus per editor can be defined here with MENU.

tools.name: SHOW
tools.description: Highlights objects and lists their details in the status bar; complete nets and signals are highlighted, and selecting a bus highlights all its nets. With forward/back annotation active, an object shown in the board is highlighted in the schematic too (cross probing) and vice versa. Useful to find parts or trace connectivity in any editor.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Object name(s); several names are highlighted together. Wildcards: * any characters, ? one character, [...] character set or range; in a schematic [n..m] is a bus range, not a wildcard.
Draws a pointer rectangle around the shown object(s) to find small objects; quote a name that is literally '@'.

tools.notes: Ctrl+Left toggles the highlight of a clicked object (several objects can be shown). If a named object is not on the current schematic sheet, a dialog lists the sheets where it was found ('-' if nowhere). You may need WINDOW FIT to see the pointer rectangle. Related: INFO.

tools.name: SIGNAL
tools.description: Defines signals in the board editor, i.e. connections between pads or smds of elements that appear as airwires in the Unrouted layer. Connections can be clicked pad by pad or given completely as text with element/pad pairs, which is how a netlist is loaded into a board that has no schematic. At least two element/pad pairs are needed.

parameters.name: signal_name
parameters.description: Name of the signal (otherwise generated).

parameters.name: element_name pad_name
parameters.description: Pairs identifying the pads/smds to connect.

tools.notes: Connecting pads that already belong to different signals opens a popup asking whether to merge them and which name to keep. The signal name _OUTLINES_ is reserved for outlines data. Related: AUTO, ROUTE, NAME, CLASS, LINE, RATSNEST, EXPORT.

tools.name: SIGNAL netlist script (board without schematic)
tools.description: A whole netlist can be entered into a board as a script file with one SIGNAL command per net, for example generated by another tool or a ULP. Place the elements first, run the script with SCRIPT, then RATSNEST to optimize the airwires before routing.
tools.usage: SIGNAL signal_name element_name pad_name element_name pad_name ..;

parameters.name: signal_name
parameters.description: Net name.

parameters.name: element_name pad_name
parameters.description: Element and pad (or smd) name pairs, at least two.

tools.notes: Use '\' at line ends to continue long pad lists. With a consistent schematic, nets should be drawn in the schematic instead (forward annotation). Related: SCRIPT, RATSNEST.

tools.name: SPLINE
tools.description: Draws a third-order spline curve, currently only in the Dimension layer, which makes it suitable for curved board outlines. Give a start point, up to two control points and an end point; to finish with fewer control points, repeat the last point.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Line width of the spline.

tools.notes: Related: LINE, ARC.

tools.name: SLICE
tools.description: Cuts lines in two along a slice line drawn with two clicks, e.g. to separate board tracks or schematic nets before re-routing them. The removed length is the larger of the slice width and twice the line width, and parts on one side of the cut can be ripped up at the same time.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Width of the cut.

parameters.name: ripup
parameters.description: None (default, no ripup), L (rip up the segments left of the slice line) or R (right of it); also available as parameter toolbar icons.

tools.notes: Left/right refer to the slice line direction from its start point to its end point. Only lines on displayed layers are cut; airwires and polygons are not sliced. Related: DELETE, RIPUP, SPLIT.

tools.name: REPOSITION
tools.description: Detaches the name, value and attribute texts of parts (schematic) or elements (board) so that they can be moved, rotated or resized like ordinary texts; this is the former SMASH function. The texts can then be put at one of nine fixed positions (Top-Left ... Bottom-Right) or anywhere with MOVE, but their content still comes from the part.
tools.usage:
REPOSITION •..
REPOSITION name ..
SMASH •..
SMASH name ..

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part or element name; for a multi-gate part in a schematic use the full instance name (part + gate).

parameters.name: Shift+Left
parameters.description: Reverses the separation ('unsmash').

tools.notes: Ctrl+Right smashes the group, Ctrl+Shift+Right unsmashes the group. Text content is changed with NAME, VALUE or ATTRIBUTE, not by editing the smashed text. Related: NAME, VALUE, TEXT, ATTRIBUTE.

tools.name: SMASH
tools.description: Older name of REPOSITION that is still listed in the syntax: it separates name, value and attribute texts from a part or element so they can be placed independently. Use REPOSITION in new scripts; the behavior is the same.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part or element to smash.

tools.notes: Shift+Left with the command active unsmashes. See REPOSITION.

tools.name: SMD
tools.description: Places surface-mount pads in a footprint in the library editor; the pad follows the cursor and each left click places one. X and Y size, roundness, orientation, flags and a name can be typed in and stay preset for following pads, and the center mouse button switches the layer (Top/Bottom). The final size on a board depends on that board's Design Rules.

parameters.name: x_width y_width
parameters.description: Pad size in the current unit, up to 200 mm (7.7840 inch).

parameters.name: -roundness
parameters.description: Integer 0..100 with a minus sign: 0 rectangular corners, 100 fully round.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: R0 ... R359.9 (see ADD); S and M not allowed.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: NOSTOP (no solder stop mask), NOTHERMALS (no thermals), NOCREAM (no cream mask).

parameters.name: 'name'
parameters.description: Pad name in single quotes; otherwise generated and changeable with NAME.

tools.notes: Right rotates the smd, Shift+Right reverses. A new SMD command resets the flags; a given flag applies to all following smds in that command. Size, roundness and flags of placed smds can be changed with CHANGE SMD width height, CHANGE ROUNDNESS value and CHANGE STOP | CREAM | THERMALS OFF | ON. A single smd on a board requires a footprint with one smd. Related: PAD, SMDARRAY, ROUTE.

tools.name: SMD roundness (round and BGA pads)
tools.description: The roundness option of SMD rounds the pad corners: -0 gives rectangles, -100 with equal X and Y size gives fully round pads as needed for BGA footprints. The minus sign distinguishes it from the size values.

parameters.name: -roundness
parameters.description: Integer 0 to 100 (percent of corner rounding).

tools.notes: The first example is the help's own (unit mil: a round 50 mil pad named 1). Combine with SMDARRAY or PATTERN for arrays.

tools.name: SMD flags and arbitrary pad shapes
tools.description: By default an smd generates solder stop mask, cream mask and thermals; the flags NOSTOP, NOCREAM and NOTHERMALS suppress them for special pads. Shapes other than rounded rectangles are made by drawing a polygon around the smd or wires whose end point is at the smd center in the same layer.

parameters.name: NOSTOP / NOCREAM / NOTHERMALS
parameters.description: Suppress solder stop mask / cream mask / thermals.

parameters.name: Polygon shape
parameters.description: Connected if the smd center lies inside the polygon's center lines; only one polygon per pad counts (more cause DRC errors).

parameters.name: Wire shape
parameters.description: Connected if a wire end point coincides with the pad center; wires attached to that wire are connected too.

tools.notes: Stop and cream masks are generated only for the pad itself; extra mask must be drawn in the mask layers. Polygons attached to a pad are ignored by the Autorouter for that signal and are obstacles for others. If a polygon/wire touches several pads, only one counts as connected (others cause DRC errors unless connected to the same pin). A C-shaped pad polygon removes orphans of board polygons inside the C regardless of the Orphans setting.

tools.name: SMDARRAY
tools.description: Creates a series of smds on one or more sides of a rectangle in the footprint editor in one step, named <base><start> to <base><start+count-1>. It can also draw a tPlace rectangle, add >NAME and >VALUE texts and delete existing smds, labels and lines first. From the SMD parameter toolbar icon a dialog opens; on the command line all arguments must be given.
tools.usage: SMDARRAY [sides base start count dx dy unit drawrect includename includevalue deleteobjs]

parameters.name: sides
parameters.description: L, R, LR, T, B or TB (Left, Right, Top, Bottom).

parameters.name: base / start / count
parameters.description: Base name, start index and number of smds.

parameters.name: dx / dy
parameters.description: Distance between smds in X and in Y direction.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: MIC, MM, MIL or INCH.

parameters.name: drawrect
parameters.description: ON/OFF: draw a rectangle in tPlace.

parameters.name: includename / includevalue
parameters.description: ON/OFF: place >NAME / >VALUE texts.

parameters.name: deleteobjs
parameters.description: ON/OFF: delete smds, labels and lines before placing.

tools.example: SMDARRAY LR P 1 8 5.4 1.27 MM ON ON ON OFF;
tools.notes: The help defines dx/dy only as X and Y distances between smds; check the result in the dialog first. Set the smd size with SMD or CHANGE SMD before. Related: SMD, PADARRAY, PINARRAY.

tools.name: SPLIT
tools.description: Splits a wire (line, track, net) or a polygon edge into two segments at the clicked point so that a bend can be introduced; the new corner can be dragged while the command is active. The shorter new segment follows the current wire bend style, the longer one runs straight to the next end point.

parameters.name: curve | @radius
parameters.description: Draws an arc as part of the new segment (see LINE).

tools.notes: Mouse: Right changes the bend style, Shift+Right reverses, Ctrl+Right toggles corresponding styles, Ctrl+Left at an end point defines an arc radius. Collinear segments are rejoined afterwards unless SET OPTIMIZING OFF is set or the wire was clicked twice at the same spot; the kept split points can be used to narrow a stretch of track (neck-down) with CHANGE WIDTH. Related: MITER, MOVE, OPTIMIZE, SLICE.

tools.name: TECHNOLOGY
tools.description: In the device editor defines the technology variants of a device, i.e. the strings that replace '*' in the device set name (74*00 becomes 74LS00, 74HCT00 ...). Names are added to the existing list, removed with '-', and all removed with -*. In the schematic or board editor TECHNOLOGY acts like CHANGE TECHNOLOGY.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Technology to add; ASCII 33..126 only, lower case converted to upper case; '' (two single quotes) is the empty technology; quote names that begin with '-'.

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Remove a technology.
Remove all technologies.

tools.notes: Only possible after a package variant has been selected with PACKAGE. In device set 74*00 the example yields 7400, 74L00, 74LS00, 74S00 and 74HCT00. The Technologies dialog lists all technologies of the library, with those of the current device checked. Technology-specific attributes are defined with ATTRIBUTE. Related: PACKAGE, 'Device name composition'.

tools.name: Device name composition (device set, technology, package variant)
tools.description: How EAGLE forms the full device name of a part from the library: '*' in the device set name is replaced by the technology and '?' by the package variant name. If the device set name contains neither, the name is device set name + technology + package variant, because the technology is processed before the package variant. The resulting name is also used as value when the device does not allow a user value (VALUE OFF).
tools.usage:
full name = device set name with '*' -> technology and '?' -> package variant
(no '*' and no '?': device_set_name + technology + package_variant)

parameters.description: Placeholder for the technology (TECHNOLOGY command).
Placeholder for the package variant (PACKAGE command); otherwise the variant is appended.

tools.example: Device set 74*00, TECHNOLOGY LS, PACKAGE variant N -> 74LS00N
tools.notes: Related: TECHNOLOGY, PACKAGE, VALUE ON/OFF, CHANGE TECHNOLOGY, VARIANT (technology per assembly variant).

tools.name: TEXT
tools.description: Places text in a drawing or a library symbol/footprint; the command stays active so several texts can be placed in a row. The orientation can be given as in ADD, the right mouse button rotates and the center button changes the layer. Size, ratio, font and alignment are set with CHANGE.

parameters.name: any_text
parameters.description: The text; enclose it in single quotes if it contains several blanks, a ';' or a word that could be taken for a command.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: R0, R90 ... (see ADD).

tools.notes: Mouse: Center selects the layer, Right rotates, Shift+Right reverses. Text is always readable from the front or the right, so after two rotations the origin moves from lower left to upper right (a text may seem unselectable); set the Spin flag for upside-down text. The reading direction of vertical text can be set in the user interface dialog. See the sub-entries for text variables, attributes, overlines, fonts/alignment and special characters. Related: CHANGE, MOVE, MIRROR, ROTATE, ATTRIBUTE.

tools.name: TEXT variables (>NAME, >VALUE, >SHEET ...)
tools.description: Texts beginning with '>' in a symbol or footprint (or on a schematic sheet/frame) are placeholders that EAGLE replaces with actual data in the schematic or board, such as the part name, value, sheet numbers, plot date or current assembly variant. They are the standard way to put names and values on symbols, packages and drawing frames.

parameters.name: >NAME / >VALUE
parameters.description: Component name (plus gate name) / value or type; only in footprints or symbols.

parameters.name: >PART / >GATE / >XREF / >CONTACT_XREF
parameters.description: Component name, gate name, part cross-reference, contact cross-reference; only in symbols.

parameters.name: >ASSEMBLY_VARIANT / >DRAWING_NAME / >LAST_DATE_TIME / >PLOT_DATE_TIME
parameters.description: Current assembly variant name, drawing name, time of last modification, time of plot creation.

parameters.name: >SHEETNR / >SHEETS / >SHEET
parameters.description: Sheet number, total sheets, and both as SHEETNR/SHEETS; only in symbols or schematics.

parameters.name: >MODULE / >SHEET_HEADLINE
parameters.description: Module name (in module sheets) and the sheet headline; symbols or schematics.

parameters.name: >SHEETNR_TOTAL / >SHEETS_TOTAL / >SHEET_TOTAL
parameters.description: Sheet number and count including module sheets.

tools.notes: The >XREF display format is set with SET XREF_PART_FORMAT (placeholders %S sheet, %C column, %R row; default '/%S.%C%R') or in Options/Set/Misc.

tools.name: TEXT attribute display (>ATTR, >ATTR=, >ATTR~, >ATTR!)
tools.description: A text '>' plus an attribute name in a symbol or footprint displays that attribute of the actual part or element. A suffix selects what is shown: nothing for the value only, '=' for name = value, '~' for the name only and '!' for nothing.

parameters.description: Show name and value.
Show only the attribute name.
Show nothing.

tools.notes: Use only one such text per attribute name in a symbol or footprint; with several, only one is displayed when the part is smashed. Attributes are defined with ATTRIBUTE.

tools.name: TEXT overline (!RESET)
tools.description: An exclamation mark before text draws it overlined, typically for active-low signal names; a second '!' ends the overline, so only part of a text can be overlined. This works in any text and in net, bus and pin names.
tools.usage:
!RESET        (whole text overlined)
!RST!/NMI     (only RST overlined)
R/!W          (only W overlined)
\!            (literal exclamation mark)

parameters.description: Starts (and a second one ends) an overline.
Escaped, non-overlining exclamation mark.

tools.notes: A '!' does not start an overline if it is the last character or is followed by a blank, a quote or a closing parenthesis, bracket or brace. After an opening '!', any unescaped '!' or ',' ends the overline (',' because of bus names).

tools.name: TEXT fonts, size, ratio, line distance and alignment
tools.description: Text appearance is controlled with CHANGE: height, stroke ratio, line distance, font and alignment (origin position). Three fonts exist (Vector, Proportional, Fixed), but the CAM Processor always outputs the built-in vector font, so use Vector for anything that goes to manufacturing.
tools.usage:
CHANGE SIZE text_size •..
CHANGE RATIO ratio •..
CHANGE LINEDISTANCE value •..
CHANGE FONT VECTOR|PROPORTIONAL|FIXED •..
CHANGE ALIGN align •..

parameters.name: SIZE
parameters.description: Text height, maximum 2 inches (thickness at most 200 mm).

parameters.name: RATIO
parameters.description: Stroke width 0...31 % of the height; only meaningful for the vector font.

parameters.name: LINEDISTANCE
parameters.description: 0...250 % of the height, for multi-line texts.

parameters.name: FONT
parameters.description: VECTOR (internal), PROPORTIONAL (e.g. Helvetica), FIXED (e.g. Courier).

parameters.name: ALIGN
parameters.description: Combination of LEFT, BOTTOM, CENTER, RIGHT, TOP (9 origins); default left bottom.

tools.notes: Non-vector fonts are drawn by the system and may differ in size; if such a text is subtracted from a signal polygon, only its bounding rectangle is subtracted. The user option 'Always vector font' (SET Interface.VectorFont 0|1) forces the vector font for display and printing; SET VECTOR_FONT OFF|ON sets the 'persistent in this drawing' flag of a board or schematic. Only ASCII characters below 128 are guaranteed to print correctly.

tools.name: TEXT special characters and multi-line text
tools.description: Rules for typing texts with blanks, semicolons, apostrophes, backslashes, line breaks or command-like words on the command line and in scripts.
tools.usage:
TEXT 'two  blanks; semicolon' •
TEXT 'it''s' •
TEXT 'line 1\nline 2' •
TEXT 'abc\\\\def' •   (gives abc\\def)

parameters.name: single quotes
parameters.description: Needed for several successive blanks, ';', or words that could be read as commands (e.g. 'red' vs REDO).
An apostrophe inside a quoted text is written doubled.

parameters.name: \n
parameters.description: Line break in the command line (Shift+Enter in the text dialog).
Each plain backslash must be escaped with another backslash.

tools.notes: Line spacing of multi-line texts: CHANGE LINEDISTANCE.

tools.name: UNDO
tools.description: Cancels previously executed commands one at a time, back to the last EDIT, OPEN or REMOVE command; REDO executes them again. It is fully integrated with forward/back annotation, so an undo applies to schematic and board together. UNDO LIST opens a dialog with the whole buffer.

parameters.name: LIST
parameters.description: Opens the undo buffer dialog (see 'UNDO LIST').

tools.notes: The undo buffer uses memory; SET UNDO_LOG OFF switches it off. RENAME and REMOVE in a library clear the buffer, as does WRITE @name. Related: REDO, SET.

tools.name: UNDO LIST (undo buffer dialog)
tools.description: Shows the entire undo buffer as a list; dragging the delimiter or clicking any step undoes (moving up) or redoes (moving down) all steps in between in order. An icon per entry shows in which drawing the command was executed. OK keeps the selected state, Cancel restores the state from before the dialog.

parameters.name: OK / Cancel
parameters.description: Keep the selected state / return to the original state.

tools.notes: Caution: after jumping far back and executing any new command, the buffer is truncated at that point and the later steps are lost for good.

tools.name: UNGROUP
tools.description: Removes persistent groups (created with NEWGROUP) from the drawing; the member objects stay in the drawing, only their group membership is removed. Works only on persistent group objects.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the persistent group.

tools.notes: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G ungroups the selected groups; the shortcut comes from default-assign.scr (the line SCRIPT default-assign.scr in Documents/EAGLE/scripts/eagle.scr must be uncommented). Related: NEWGROUP, EDITGROUP, Groups view in the Design Manager.

tools.name: UPDATE
tools.description: Compares the parts of a board or schematic with their library objects and updates them automatically when the library version differs; with forward/back annotation active both drawings are updated. Without parameters a dialog selects the library; with a bare ';' all parts are checked; with library names only parts from those libraries. In the library editor it updates footprints of the open library from other libraries.

parameters.name: library_name
parameters.description: Plain name ('ttl' or 'ttl.lbr'), full or relative file name, or the URN of a downloaded managed library; quote names with blanks.

parameters.name: footprint_name@library_name
parameters.description: Library editor: update only this footprint.
Append / strip an '@number' suffix to local library names (see 'UPDATE library rename').

parameters.name: old_library_name = new_library_name
parameters.description: Update a library of the drawing from a differently named library and rename it.

tools.notes: Matching: same URN (managed) or same name without URN (local) first, then same name where one side has no URN; different URNs never match; names are case insensitive and paths are ignored unless given. Missing libraries are skipped (errors only for libraries named on the command line). If objects were renamed and moved at once, the update may fail; do it in two steps. Run DRC and ERC afterwards. Not allowed while an assembly variant is active. Related: ADD, REPLACE, USE.

tools.name: UPDATE library rename (old = new) and @ suffixes (+@ / -@)
tools.description: UPDATE old = new locates the library named old in the current board or schematic, updates it with the contents of new and then renames it, which is how a drawing is switched to a renamed or relocated library. UPDATE +@ appends '@' and a number to local library names so that later adding parts from a newer library of the same name does not modify the existing ones; UPDATE -@ removes these suffixes again.

parameters.name: old_library_name
parameters.description: Pure library name as stored in the drawing (no path).

parameters.name: new_library_name
parameters.description: Full path name or URN allowed; must not yet be used in the drawing.
For the given libraries or, without names, all libraries.

tools.notes: There must be at least one blank before and after '='. +@ does not change names that already end in @number, nor managed library names; -@ only works if no local library with the resulting name exists. UPDATE +@; followed by UPDATE -@; does not necessarily restore the original names.

tools.name: UPDATE in a library (footprint@library)
tools.description: In the library editor, UPDATE replaces all footprints of the open library with the versions from the given libraries, or only a specific footprint with footprint_name@library_name. Useful to propagate a corrected footprint into libraries that contain copies of it.

parameters.name: library_name
parameters.description: Source library for all matching footprints.

parameters.name: footprint_name@library_name
parameters.description: Only this footprint from that library.

tools.notes: Related: UPDATE, COPY footprint@library.

tools.name: USE
tools.description: Marks libraries for use by ADD and REPLACE, or drops them again. Without parameters it opens the library management dialog, which also downloads and updates managed libraries. Parts are copied completely into the drawing when added, so the drawing does not need the library later and library changes do not affect it until UPDATE.

parameters.name: library_name
parameters.description: Library name (wildcards allowed, .lbr optional), URN of a downloaded managed library, or a directory (marks all libraries in it).

parameters.name: -library_name
parameters.description: Drop this library.
Drop all previously marked libraries.

tools.notes: Libraries can also be marked in the Control Panel via their activation icon or the 'Use' context menu entry (all/none from the 'Libraries' entry). The libraries in use are stored in the project file when a project is open. Related: ADD, REPLACE, UPDATE.

tools.name: VALUE
tools.description: Shows or changes the value of parts and elements (e.g. 10k, 100nF) in schematic and board. Typing a value first and then clicking several parts gives all of them that value; name/value pairs set values directly, which is convenient in scripts. It works only in the default assembly variant; other variants are edited with VARIANT.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: New value applied to every subsequently clicked part.

parameters.name: name value
parameters.description: Part/element name and value pairs, repeatable.

parameters.name: ON / OFF
parameters.description: Device editor only (see 'VALUE ON / OFF').

tools.notes: The '\' at line ends keeps the next line from being read as a command keyword. The warning when a part has no user-definable value can be disabled with the eaglerc parameter Warning.PartHasNoUserDefinableValue; Sch.Cmd.Add.AlwaysUseDeviceNameAsValue uses the device name as value. Related: NAME, REPOSITION, VARIANT.

tools.name: VALUE ON / OFF (device editor)
tools.description: In the device editor, decides whether parts made from this device get a user-editable value. ON lets the value be set freely in the schematic (resistors, capacitors); OFF enters the device name automatically as value (e.g. 74LS00N) and a user change needs confirmation.

parameters.name: ON
parameters.description: Value can be changed in the schematic.

parameters.name: OFF
parameters.description: Value is the full device name; changing it requires confirmation.

tools.notes: VARIANT can only set a per-variant value if the device set has the user value enabled. Related: TECHNOLOGY, PACKAGE, 'Device name composition'.

tools.name: VARIANT
tools.description: Manages assembly variants in the schematic: which parts are populated in a given variant and which value and technology they have there. Giving only a variant name switches the whole project to that variant, and an empty name ('') returns to the default (as if there were no variants). Without parameters a dialog manages all variants.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Variant name, case insensitive; quote it if it contains blanks, '+' or '-'.

parameters.name: part_name POPULATE | NOPOPULATE
parameters.description: Mark the part populated or not populated in that variant (creating the variant entry for the part).

parameters.name: value [technology]
parameters.description: Optional per-variant value (only if the device set allows a user value) and technology (schematic only); use '' for the value to set only a technology.

parameters.name: +name / -name
parameters.description: Create a new variant (nothing happens if it exists) / delete a variant; name '*' with '-' deletes all (with confirmation unless in a script).

tools.notes: Unpopulated parts are crossed out (X) in the schematic, and their placement items (place layers, names, values) are not drawn in the board; Option.UnpopulatedMarkScaling scales the X. >ASSEMBLY_VARIANT displays the current variant. ADD, CHANGE PACKAGE | TECHNOLOGY, REPLACE, UPDATE and VALUE only work with no variant active; COPY does not copy variant data; a drawing always loads in the default variant. In the board VARIANT is not supported (controlled from the schematic); standalone boards use CHANGE POPULATE. The CAM Processor can output a variant (eaglecon -A).

tools.name: VARIANT module assembly variants
tools.description: Modules in hierarchical schematics have their own assembly variants, independent of the main schematic's variants; each module instance selects which module variant it uses. On a module's sheets the VARIANT command refers to that module's variants, on main sheets to the main assembly variants.
tools.usage: VARIANT name part_name [NO]POPULATE [ value [ technology ] ];   (while editing a module sheet)

parameters.name: Module assembly variant
parameters.description: Variant defined inside a module.

parameters.name: Main assembly variant
parameters.description: Variant defined on the main schematic sheets.

tools.notes: VARIANT is not meant for switching a module's variant; the variant used by a module instance is selected per instance. Related: MODULE, VARIANT.

tools.name: VIA
tools.description: Places vias in the board editor; the via follows the cursor and each left click places one. A via placed on an existing wire joins that signal, and EAGLE asks before connecting different signals. Diameter, shape, layer span and flags can be typed in and stay preset; the final size and shape follow the board's Design Rules.

parameters.name: 'signal_name'
parameters.description: For scripts that read generated data: all following vias join this signal without automatic checks (risk of shorts; run DRC).

parameters.name: diameter
parameters.description: Outer diameter in the current unit, up to 200 mm; the drill is the one set for pads (CHANGE DRILL).

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Square, Round or Octagon (outer layers; inner layers always round).

parameters.name: layers
parameters.description: Span from-to, e.g. 2-7 (same as 7-2) for blind/buried vias; if that exact span is not in the Design Rules layer setup, the next longer via is used or an error is issued.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: STOP forces a solder stop mask; by default vias with drill <= Design Rules Masks/Limit get none.

tools.notes: Vias create drill symbols in the Drills layer and stop mask in tStop/bStop. SET Option.ViaLength 1 prints the layer span on each via. Vias have no element name and do not appear in the netlist. Related: PAD, SMD, CHANGE, DISPLAY, ROUTE (vias placed automatically on layer change).

tools.name: WINDOW
tools.description: Zooms and pans the drawing view in any editor. With ';' it redraws, one point sets a new center, two points zoom to a rectangle and three points set center and zoom ratio; a number scales the view, FIT shows the whole drawing, LAST returns to the previous view and FLIP shows the board from the bottom side.

parameters.name: scale_factor
parameters.description: Zoom factor around the current center (2 = twice as large, 0.5 = half).

parameters.name: FIT
parameters.description: Fit the entire drawing into the window.

parameters.name: LAST
parameters.description: Previous window selection (zoom-only commands and mouse changes are not stored).

parameters.name: FLIP
parameters.description: View and edit the board from the bottom side.
Three points: new center, then zoom in if point 3 is farther from point 1 than point 2, zoom out if it lies between.

tools.notes: Keys: Alt+F2 = WINDOW FIT, F2 = WINDOW; (redraw), F3 = WINDOW 2, F4 = WINDOW 0.5, F5 = WINDOW (@); (cursor becomes center). Left&Drag defines a zoom rectangle. Commands with fewer than three clicks must end with ';'. Zoom is limited to about a 1 mm field unless 'Options/User interface/Limit zoom factor' is unchecked; at extreme zoom non-vector texts may vanish and arcs are approximated. See also 'WINDOW parameter aliases'.

tools.name: WINDOW parameter aliases
tools.description: Named aliases store WINDOW parameters (for example a board region) so that a view can be recalled by name. They are also listed when the 'WINDOW Select' button is held down or right-clicked.
tools.usage:
WINDOW = name parameters
WINDOW = name @
WINDOW = ?
WINDOW = name
WINDOW = name;
WINDOW name

parameters.name: = name parameters
parameters.description: Define alias name to expand to the given parameters.

parameters.name: = name @
parameters.description: Define the alias as the current window selection.
Ask for a name for the current window settings.

parameters.name: = name
parameters.description: Let the user select a window area that becomes the alias.

parameters.name: = name;
parameters.description: Delete the alias.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Execute the alias; may be abbreviated and combined with other parameters or aliases.

tools.notes: Alias names consist of letters, digits and underscores, start with a letter or underscore, are case insensitive and must not be option keywords; an abbreviated alias takes precedence over parameter names.

tools.name: WIRE
tools.description: Deprecated keyword: the WIRE command has been renamed to LINE, which draws lines and routed tracks. Use LINE in new scripts and replace WIRE in old ones.
tools.notes: Some eaglerc parameters still use the old name, e.g. Cmd.Wire.IgnoreCtrlForRadiusMode. Related: LINE, ROUTE.

tools.name: WRITE
tools.description: Saves the current drawing, library or design block. With a name (optionally with a path; default is the project directory) the file is saved under that name; with @name the loaded drawing itself is renamed, its board/schematic partner is saved under the new name as well and the UNDO buffer is cleared. For forward/back annotation consistency, saving under the same name also saves a modified partner drawing, and saving under a new name asks whether to save the partner too.
tools.usage:
WRITE;
WRITE name
WRITE @name
WRITE 7 [ name ]
WRITE [ DBL ] name

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Save a copy under this name (the modified flag of the loaded drawing is not cleared).

parameters.name: @name
parameters.description: Rename the loaded drawing (and its partner) and save.
Save in EAGLE 7.x format (see 'WRITE 7').

parameters.name: DBL
parameters.description: Save a design block (see 'WRITE DBL').

tools.notes: Chosen from the menu, WRITE asks for the file name (Escape/Cancel aborts). In automated runs save with WRITE; before QUIT to avoid the save prompt. Related: EDIT, QUIT, CLOSE.

tools.name: WRITE 7 (save for EAGLE 7.x)
tools.description: Saves the drawing(s) in a form that EAGLE 7.x can open: XML attributes introduced with EAGLE 8 are omitted and other adjustments are made. Use it to exchange designs with users or tools that only read the EAGLE 7 format.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Target file; without it a file dialog asks for one.

tools.notes: Some information is lost, e.g. managed library URNs and their assets. The @name form is not supported with WRITE 7.

tools.name: WRITE DBL (design block) and Save selection as Design Block
tools.description: WRITE DBL generates a design block from the loaded schematic and/or board (depending on the editor and on whether the pair is consistent) and saves it for reuse with PASTE DBL. Without a name a dialog opens with a preview, an HTML description field, editable and generated attributes and the file location. File > 'Save selection as Design Block' saves only a selected part of the design.
tools.usage:
WRITE [ DBL ] name
File > Save selection as Design Block

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Design block file name (saved in the design block directory if no path is given).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Additive selection in the first editor (Ctrl+click deselects), finished with Ctrl+Right click; with both editors open the selection continues in the second editor with the counterparts preselected, finished again with Ctrl+Right click.

tools.notes: Selection rules: started from a board with a multi-sheet schematic, only objects with counterparts on the current sheet; net segments must be selected completely (wires and labels); all instances of each part; all part instances connected to a selected net segment. Objects that would break consistency are filtered out in the second editor, while non-electrical objects (texts, dimensions) and routed wires/polygons of selected nets can be added. Not yet supported in hierarchical designs. Design blocks are previewed with EDIT name.dbl.
